newsitem.title: USA: IVAX kidney drug preclinicals promising.
newsitem.headline: IVAX kidney drug preclinicals promising.

text.p: IVAX Corp said on Monday that in preclinical animal and in vitro studies, its oral compound Elmiron (pentosan polysulfate sodium) stopped or reversed glomerular scarring in the kidney and significantly reduced vascular scarring caused by atherosclerosis (hardening of the arteries).
The studies were conducted in collaboration with the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases of the National Institutes of Health.
IVAX said that the data suggest that Elmiron inhibits scarring related to abnormalities in the smooth muscle cells in the aorta and in the blood vessels of the kidney.
A similar scarring process in humans has previously been considered to be progressive and irreversible, leading to severe atherosclerosis and kidney failure.

In September 1996, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted IVAX clearance to market Elmiron for the relief of the pain or discomfort associated with the debilitating urinary bladder disease known as interstitial cystitis.
